c.tagline: A Caribbean island escape of turquoise 'sea of seven colors' waters and Raizal island culture

card: Widely accepted at hotels and larger restaurants; cash useful for beach vendors and small shops

taxi.fare: Fixed zone-based fares rather than metered
taxi.fareNote: San Andrés taxis charge set rates by zone; confirm the fare before departure

emergency.note: 123 connects to police, fire, and medical services across Colombia

religion: Christianity (Roman Catholic majority, strong Protestant/Baptist presence tied to Raizal heritage)
walk: The town center (El Centro) is walkable, but San Luis, West View, and La Loma require a golf cart, moto-taxi, or car to reach

safety.safety: Generally safe and tourism-oriented; standard beach-destination precautions apply
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches is the main concern

hood_landmark.West View: West View's cliff-jumping and snorkeling cove
hood_landmark.La Loma: La Loma's hilltop First Baptist Church
hood_landmark.Sound Bay / North End Beaches: The main North End tourist beach strip

avoid.reason: Stay out of the inland residential barrios away from the tourist strip after dark, where occasional gang-related crime occurs.
Watch belongings on busy Spratt Bight beach, decline street drug offers firmly, and agree rental and water-sport prices in advance.

hood_desc: The compact commercial hub with shops, restaurants, and the main hotel strip; the natural base for most visitors.
A quieter stretch of beach on the island's east side, popular with locals and travelers wanting fewer crowds.
A rocky cove on the island's west side known for cliff-jumping and calm snorkeling waters.
A hilltop Raizal community with island views and a historic Baptist church, offering a glimpse of local culture beyond the beach resorts.
The lively main tourist beach along the North End, lined with hotels, bars, and water-sports operators.

water.note: Fresh water is scarce on the island; drink bottled water only.

transit.sys: Golf cart rentals, moto-taxis, and small buses circling the island's ring road
transit.pay: Cash fares for buses and moto-taxis; golf carts rented by the day
transit.map: Not centrally published; the island's single ring road makes navigation simple
transit.note: Renting a golf cart is the most popular way for visitors to get around the island

transport.air: Gustavo Rojas Pinilla International Airport (ADZ), about 10 min from town
transport.bus: Small local buses circle the island's ring road
transport.ferry: Catamaran ferry service to Providencia island
transport.car: Rental cars, scooters, and golf carts are available for the island's compact ring road

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels
net.ap: A Claro or Movistar tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is often added automatically ('propina voluntaria') at restaurants; check the bill
tip.r: 10% is customary if not already included
